key_insight: A diffusion inpainting approach can turn abnormal mammograms into realistic healthy counterfactuals to improve breast cancer classifier training.
clinical_relevance: This may reduce false negatives in CAD systems by making models more sensitive to missed lesions, especially at high specificity settings.
method: Train a DDPM on BI-RADS 1 healthy mammograms
Use RePaint-based inpainting to replace annotated lesion boxes with normal tissue
Augment training for ConvNeXt, ViT, Mammo-CLIP, and FPN-MIL classifiers
evidence_signal: On VinDr-Mammo, counterfactual augmentation improved sensitivity across all four evaluated architectures, including at 80% fixed specificity, and generated images were judged realistic by radiologists.
watch_item: Results are based on a specific dataset and annotated bounding boxes, so performance and realism may vary when lesions are poorly localized or when deployed on different screening populations.
paper_title: Healthy Counterfactual Generation via Diffusion Inpainting for Mammography Classification
